summary: Aggressive SDK retry + socket reuse interacting with keepalive causing client-side queueing and elevated P95 latency
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent spikes in end-to-end inference P95 latency (and some client-side request timeouts) beginning 2026-03-04. PineApps is on Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 and uses our official Node + Python SDKs. Impact: user-facing feature slowdown and sporadic 504-like timeouts from SDKs. Environment: prod (dedicated pool ID: ded-32-a), client SDK versions node 3.2.1, python 2.9.0. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run sustained bursty traffic from multiple client instances (50-200 concurrent connections) with short TTL per request, 2) Observe elevated client-side latency P95 and occasional SDK timeouts while server-side RT metrics (token generation time) remain normal. Logs/observations: SDK logs show repeated connection resets and retry backoff chains. Kernel traces on customer's side show many sockets in TIME_WAIT with keepalive probes. API gateway metrics: increased connection churn but stable generation latency on the serving runtime. Initial mitigation: recommended SDK version pin to latest (where we've changed default retry delays) and increased client-side connection pool size as a temporary workaround.
comments: 2026-03-05 09:12 - Asha Patel: Customer reported high P95 on calls to /v1/generate; attached sample traces and SDK logs. They see ~2-3x baseline P95 bursts and intermittent request errors from the client. Asked for request ids and pool details.

2026-03-05 10:01 - Marco Hernandez (SRE): Collected gateway metrics and CPU on dedicated hosts. Serving runtime shows consistent per-request token times. No obvious backend queueing. Requested tcpdump from customer and SDK config (keepalive, maxSockets, retry settings).

2026-03-05 14:28 - PineApps (Customer): Attached tcpdump and SDK config. Node SDK set maxSockets=6, keepAlive=true, keepAliveMsecs=60000, retry policy: exponential with initialDelay=200ms, maxRetries=6. Multiple app instances behind a load balancer.

2026-03-06 08:46 - Marco Hernandez: Reproduced locally with their config. Observed that when retries back off and sockets are reused aggressively, client threads block waiting for socket availability. With maxSockets low and long keepalive, the SDK queues requests locally rather than opening new sockets due to ephemeral port exhaustion and TIME_WAIT growth from churn. Not a server-side backlog.

2026-03-07 11:02 - Eng (SDK team) - Mei Chen: Confirmed Node SDK prior to 3.2.5 had a bug where exponential backoff jitter was too conservative combined with agent keepalive behavior. Opened PR to change default maxSockets and add adaptive backoff jitter. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rumble/pull/456

2026-03-09 15:20 - Marco Hernandez: Deployed mitigation to customer: recommended immediate client-side changes: set maxSockets=50, reduce keepAliveMsecs to 10000, lower initial retry delay to 100ms and cap maxRetries to 3. After these changes, customer reports P95 returned to baseline and no further client-side timeouts.

2026-03-10 09:41 - PineApps (Customer): Confirmed fix holds under load tests (up to 500 RPS sustained). Happy to keep Dedicated pool but requested a formal SDK patch and release notes so their ops can update confidently.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Mei Chen (SDK): Released Node SDK 3.2.5 with adaptive jitter and safer defaults; added explicit guidance to docs for connection pooling under high concurrency. Python SDK release planned next week.
2026-03-10 10:20 - Asha Patel: Marking as resolved. Follow-up task created to add a troubleshooting guide to Console KB and include recommended pool defaults in quickstart templates.
investigation_notes: Observed discrepancy between client perceived latency and backend token-generation time. Server-side P95 for generation stayed within SLOs while client-side P95 spiked.
Packet captures from customer showed many short-lived TCP connections and high TIME_WAIT counts; connection churn increased under bursts.
Customer's SDK maxSockets was low (6) which, combined with aggressive retry attempts, caused local queueing in the SDK when sockets were briefly unavailable.
Keepalive with long intervals meant idle sockets persisted, preventing ephemeral port reuse and causing the client to open/close sockets more frequently when pool size was exceeded.

Reproduction notes: With a synthetic client mimicking customer's concurrency and original SDK config, reproduces increased client-side P95 within ~10 minutes of sustained bursts. After changing pool/defaults reproduction stops.

Root cause: Interaction of conservative retry/backoff config + small connection pool + long TCP keepalive => client-side request queueing and exponential backoff retries that multiplied perceived latency. Secondary factor: some customer app instances had periodic restarts causing ephemeral port churn.
Server-side mitigations were unnecessary; issue fixed by SDK defaults and customer config changes. Confirmed no resource leaks in serving runtime.
Related symptoms: similar pattern referenced in SUP-12903 and SUP-8419 but root cause here was adaptive jitter + pool sizing rather than server throttling.
resolution: Root cause: misaligned client SDK defaults (small maxSockets, long keepalive, conservative retry backoff) causing local queueing and perceived latency increases. Resolution delivered: 1) Customer applied immediate config workaround (increase maxSockets, reduce keepAliveMsecs, cap retries). 2) Node SDK 3.2.5 released with adaptive backoff jitter and updated default pool sizes. 3) Added KB entry and Console quickstart note with recommended SDK connection-pool and retry settings for Dedicated pools. 4) Follow-up: Python SDK patch scheduled and outreach to all Dedicated customers about recommended SDK tuning. No server-side change required.
